name: Pedal Hi-Hat
notes:
REBUILT 2026-09-28 as a MODAL PLATE with collision RATTLE (see
gen_cymbal_modal in modular_stages.c) against a user-supplied acoustic
closed hi-hat. The legacy variant-0 voice was six square oscillators plus
flat white noise: measured on the reference it was all wrong in the way that
reads "electronic" — spectral flatness 0.006 (six tones) where the real hat
is 0.29 (noise-like), energy flat to 20 kHz where the real hat centres on
8-12 kHz and rolls off above 14 kHz, and a peak at 0.4 ms where the real hat
swells over ~8 ms and holds a CHATTERING ~40 ms plateau before it decays.

That plateau is the physics of a hi-hat (Sekiguchi & Samejima 2023): two
cymbals clamped together, the top one re-colliding with the bottom after the
stick hit. The voice models it directly — the plate's impulse response
re-struck by a decaying Poisson train of collision impulses — so the noise
is the plate itself rattling, not a noise generator.

FITTED on the real C render: 1/3-octave x time energy map (1-16 kHz, 0-320
ms) + the 2 ms envelope over the first 60 ms + spectral flatness, minimized
by coordinate descent. Score 4.1 against 32 for the legacy voice on the same
measure. Units: env_tail / env_fast Np/s, *_f Hz, *_w octaves, rattle_rate
collisions/s, rattle_decay s.

Chosen BY EAR (2026-09-28) from five fitted takes: this is "H4 — tight"
(rattle_decay 0.058 -> 0.042, env_tail 28 -> 36); the looser takes were
judged "too low pitched". The fit's best-scoring take (4.1) was the looser
H1; the ear preferred the tighter chick.

Shared by hihat, hihat-lofi and hihat-pedal (each keeps its own DefaultFX).

finish.notes: out_clamp: no output limit (these voices never had one)
